transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. Um, I guess... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but what brings me in is that I’m having a little trouble keeping my words in a straight line lately. 

It’s probably just me being a little tired from work, I don't want to make a huge deal out of it, but... like, I’ll start talking to the nurses about my overnight shift, and then somehow I end up jumping to soccer, or... or paint colors on the wall, and then patient charts. And I can just see everyone getting lost while I'm talking. It's really embarrassing, honestly. I try so hard to be clear and do a good job, I promise. 

Does... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you needed to know?

Can you tell me more about how your thoughts move from one idea to another when you're talking? Do you feel like your thoughts are jumping around even inside your head, or do they make sense to you at the time?

Um... yeah, like I was just saying with the... the words getting all jumbled up? Inside my head, it honestly feels like it makes perfect sense at the time. I really hope I'm not sounding, you know, crazy or anything. I don't want you to think badly of me. 

But to me, it's all connected. Like, I'll be thinking about the overnight shift, and that reminds me of how tired I was playing soccer, and the soccer ball is white just like the paint on the wall, and the wall is right next to where we keep the patient charts. So it makes total sense to me, I swear. But when I actually talk, I guess I accidentally skip over all those middle parts? And then I just see the nurses staring at me, and I realize I lost them again. 

I try so hard to catch myself because I don't want to bother anyone or make them think I can't do my job. I'm a really good aide, I promise, I always get my rounds done. I just... I get a little tangled up sometimes. Did... did I explain that right? Is that what you meant?
When you're thinking to yourself, like when you're alone or trying to organize your day, do your thoughts ever feel disorganized or hard to follow, even inside your own head?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I can't think at all, because I really do try my best to stay on top of things. But... sometimes, yeah, it gets a little foggy in there. 

Like, if I'm trying to read a patient note or... or even just looking at a bill at home, I might read the same page two or three times and still not really get what it says. It's probably just because I'm working so hard and getting tired, you know? And... sometimes even little things, like trying to pick what to buy at the grocery store, I just kind of... freeze up. I can't figure out what to choose. 

I'm really sorry, I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. I still get all my work done, I promise. Does... does everyone get like that sometimes when they're tired? Is that an okay answer?
Have you ever experienced hearing voices or seeing things that others don't hear or see? Or have you ever had any unusual beliefs that other people might find strange?

Um... no, no voices or anything like that. I don't see things that aren't there, I promise. I know that would be really bad, and I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my mind or that I can't work with the patients. 

But... well, I guess... I don't know if this is what you mean by an unusual belief, and I really hope this doesn't sound paranoid, because I'm usually a very trusting person. But lately, I've just been... well, I'm pretty sure the supervisors have been changing my shifts on purpose. And... and I think they're watching me through the unit cameras. 

Like, I know the other aides say it's just normal staffing shortages when my schedule gets moved around, and they tell me the cameras are just for patient safety. And I want to believe them, I really do. But it just feels like... like they're specifically watching *me*, to see if I'm being unsafe or doing something wrong. 

I try so hard to be perfect on the floor so they won't have any reason to think I'm a bad aide. I really care about my job. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm not overreacting, I just want to be honest with you. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your head by someone else, or that your thoughts are being broadcast out for others to hear?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely nothing like that. I've never felt like someone was putting thoughts in my head, or... or that people could hear what I'm thinking. That sounds really scary, honestly. 

I mean, I know I just said I feel like the supervisors are watching me on the cameras, but it's not like they're in my head or anything. It's just normal thoughts, you know? Just me worrying about my job and wanting to do well. I definitely don't think my thoughts are being broadcast. I keep everything to myself, I promise. 

I really hope my answers are okay. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you know I'm still doing a good job at work. Did I... did I answer that right?
Have you ever felt that things happening around you, like things on TV, in the news, or things people say or do, are specifically directed at you or have a special meaning for you?

Um... no, no, I don't think so. I don't really watch a lot of TV anyway, to be honest. Mostly I just come home from the hospital and try to rest so I'm ready for my next shift. 

I definitely don't think the news is about me or anything like that. I know I'm just a regular person, just an aide trying to help out on the unit. I wouldn't ever think that things on TV were sending me messages or anything. That would be pretty strange, right? 

I just try to mind my own business and do my work. I hope that's the right answer... I just want to be as helpful as I can. Is that okay?
Outside of work and conversations, do you ever find it hard to stay organized with your daily tasks at home, like keeping track of appointments, managing your time, or completing chores?

Um... well... I guess things have been a little tough at home lately. I mean, I'm usually really good about keeping things neat, but... I don't know, I guess I've fallen behind on some things. My apartment's gotten a bit messy, and... I think I missed a few bills. I haven't really been talking to my friends much either. I just... I get so tired, you know? 

And, um... I really hate to admit this, because I want you to know I'm usually very responsible, but... at work, I've had to ask some of my coworkers to double-check my rounds and my charting. Just to be safe! I want to make sure I'm doing everything perfectly for the patients. I know that probably sounds bad, but I just want to be thorough. 

Actually, um... things got a little overwhelming recently. I went to employee health because... well, I was just feeling so down, and I accidentally mentioned that I was having some... some really dark thoughts. Like, about not wanting to be here anymore. About suicide. And they sent me for an emergency evaluation. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds terrible. I really don't want you to think I'm incapable or that I can't do my job. I'm trying so hard to get back on track. Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I shared that with you... I just want to be completely honest so you can help me be a good aide again. Is that what you needed to know?
Can you tell me more about those dark thoughts you mentioned—how often they come up, and if you’ve felt this way before?

Um... well, they don't happen all the time, I promise. It's mostly just... after a really bad night, you know? When I haven't slept well or work was really stressful. I just... I keep thinking it would be easier if I didn't wake up. 

It's not like I want to do anything bad, but... sometimes the thought comes that I should just end it. But I always get really scared when that happens! That's why I went to employee health and told someone. Because I know it's wrong to think that way, and I want to be safe. 

I've never really felt this bad before, it's just been lately with everything feeling so heavy. I'm really trying to push past it, though. I know I need to be strong for my patients. I hope... I hope you don't think less of me for having those thoughts. I did the right thing by telling someone, didn't I?

Can you tell me if there are times when you start doing something, like a task at work or even something at home, but then you lose track of what you were trying to accomplish or find yourself doing something completely different without meaning to?

Um... well... I guess, yeah, sometimes I do get a little... sidetracked? I mean, I really try to stay focused, I promise. But... 

I don't know, it's embarrassing to admit, but sometimes at work... I've caught myself doing things that are kind of strange. Like, I'll be in the hallway, and I'll realize I'm just... rocking back and forth. Or... there was this one time I caught myself copying a patient who was tapping on the wall. I didn't even mean to do it, it just sort of happened! 

And sometimes... well, sometimes I'll be getting ready to do my rounds, and I'll just be standing there with my gloves half on, like I'm completely stuck. I know I'm supposed to be checking on everyone, but my body just kind of stops. 

I'm really sorry, I know that probably sounds so unprofessional for an aide to do. I really don't want to be a burden on the unit, and I'm trying so hard to keep it together. I know I shouldn't be acting like that. Do you think... do you think that's something we can fix? I just want to do a good job.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being taken out of your head or like certain things happening around you have a special hidden meaning meant only for you?

Um... no, not like thoughts being taken away or... hidden meanings. Nothing crazy like that, I promise. But... 

Well, I do worry sometimes about... about work. I know they say it's just staffing shortages, but... I'm pretty sure the supervisors have been changing my shifts on purpose. And... I know this sounds a little paranoid, and I really try not to think about it, but... I feel like they're watching me through the unit cameras. 

Just to see if I'm being unsafe, you know? Because of what happened at employee health. I mean, it makes sense that they'd want to keep an eye on me, right? They have to protect the patients. I don't blame them at all! I just... I wish they would trust me a little more. I'm really trying to be careful and do everything right. 

I know it's probably just my anxiety acting up, and I shouldn't jump to conclusions. I'm sorry if that sounds bad or if I shouldn't have brought it up. I just want to be honest with you. Is it normal to feel a little watched after something like that happens? I just want to be a good employee again.
Have you ever felt that random events or gestures around you, like people talking, phone calls, or everyday occurrences, were secretly about you or had a special meaning for you?

Um... no, no, I don't think so. I mean, I know sometimes people talk in the breakroom and I might wonder if they're talking about me, but... that's just normal insecurity, right? Like, I don't think random things are secretly about me or anything like that. 

I know some of the patients on the unit get like that, where they think the TV is talking to them or something, but I promise I don't have anything like that going on. I'm just... I just get a little worried about what people think of me, especially the supervisors. But that's not the same thing, is it? I hope I'm making sense. I really don't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or anything. I'm just trying to be self-aware. That's a good thing, right?
Have you ever felt like certain things people do, like their actions or conversations, are secretly sending you messages or have a hidden meaning that only you understand?

Oh, um... no. No, I don't experience anything like that. I know you asked something kind of similar just a moment ago, and I'm really sorry if I didn't explain myself well enough the first time! I promise I'm really paying attention to your questions. 

But no, if I see people talking or doing things, I don't think there's a secret message in it for me. I mean, like I said, I might worry if they're talking about my job performance, but I don't think anyone is speaking in code or sending me special signals or anything. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have that going on. I really want to be helpful and give you the right answers so we can figure everything out. Am I doing okay with these questions? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you used to like?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? But I think that's pretty normal when you're stressed, right? Like, I used to do a lot more stuff... I'd sketch murals, and I really liked cooking for my friends. We used to play soccer on the weekends, too. 

Lately, though... I don't know, it just feels kind of pointless? I guess I've been staying in my apartment a lot more and ignoring messages. But it's just because I've been so tired from worrying about work, you know? It's not like I'm trying to be a bad friend or anything! I just... I need to rest so I can go back to being a good employee. 

I'm sure once things settle down at the hospital, I'll get back to all my hobbies. It's okay to take a break from things sometimes, isn't it? I really hope I don't sound lazy... I promise I'm usually a really active person.
Have you noticed that you're speaking more quickly than usual, or that you feel a strong pressure to keep talking even when others are trying to respond?

Oh, um, no... I don't think so. I mean, I know I'm probably talking a lot right now, and I'm really sorry if I'm rambling or taking up too much of your time! I just get a little nervous in these kinds of interviews, you know? I want to make sure I'm giving you all the details you need. 

But I don't feel like I *have* to keep talking, or like my thoughts are racing so fast I can't stop. I'm just trying to be thorough. I usually listen a lot more than I talk, especially at work. You have to be a good listener when you're an orderly, right? 

I promise I'll try to keep my answers shorter if that helps! I really don't want to overwhelm you. Am I talking too fast right now? I can slow down, just let me know.
Have you found yourself starting tasks but then losing track of the goal, like you forget why you began doing something or get distracted in a way that makes the task itself fall apart?

Well, um... maybe a little bit? But I think it's just because it gets so busy at the hospital, you know? Anyone would get a little distracted. 

I mean, I guess sometimes... I'll be in the middle of something and just kind of... stop. Like, the other day I was putting my gloves on for rounds, and I just sort of stood there with them half on, like I was stuck. And I know I shouldn't do this, but sometimes I catch myself rocking back and forth in the hallway, or even copying a patient when they're tapping on something. 

I'm really trying to stop doing that, I promise! I know it doesn't look professional, and I really want to be a good orderly. It's just hard to stay focused sometimes when I'm so worried about everything. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm bad at my job... I really do try my best. Is it normal to get a little side-tracked like that when you're stressed out?
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are not your own, or that someone else is putting thoughts into your mind?

Oh, no, definitely not! I mean, that sounds really scary, doesn't it? Having someone else put thoughts in your head? 

I... I don't have anything like that happening. My thoughts are just my own. Mostly just me worrying about work and trying to make sure I'm doing everything right. Sometimes I get a little overwhelmed, but it's just regular stress, I promise. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or anything like that. I know how important it is to stay grounded, especially working where I do. So, no, nothing like that at all. That's a good thing, right? I mean, it means I'm still doing okay in that department, at least?
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being influenced by something outside of yourself, or like everyday things around you have a special hidden message meant only for you?

Um, hidden messages? No, definitely not from everyday things. I know that would be a bad sign, right? I try really hard to keep a level head. 

But... well, I guess there is one thing at work that's been making me a little anxious, if it's okay to mention? My supervisors have been changing my shifts around a lot lately. And, um, everyone keeps telling me it's just because of the staffing shortages we've been having. I know I should just accept that, and I really don't want to sound like a complainer! 

But... I'm just so sure they're doing it on purpose. And... please don't think I'm weird for saying this, but I'm pretty sure they watch me through the unit cameras, too. Just to see if I'm being unsafe or messing up. I mean, they have to monitor the cameras anyway for the patients, right? So it kind of makes sense they'd watch me too... I just want to prove to them that I'm doing a good job and that I'm safe. 

It's normal to worry about your bosses keeping an eye on you, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm not overthinking it. I really do want to be a good employee for them.

Have you ever felt that random or neutral things people do, like their conversations, actions, or things you see around you, are actually about you or meant for you, even if others don’t see it that way?

Oh, no, not at all. I mean, I know some of the patients at the hospital get like that, where they think the TV is talking to them or that people walking by are whispering about them. But I definitely don't have anything like that going on. 

I know it's important to know the difference between what's real and what's not, and I really try to stay focused on my actual work. If people are talking, I just figure they're talking about their own stuff, you know? I wouldn't want to assume everything is about me, that seems a little self-centered, doesn't it? 

I just try to keep my head down and do my job. I'm doing the right thing by just ignoring other people's conversations, right? I really don't want to cause any trouble or make anyone think I'm being paranoid. I'm just trying to be a good orderly.
Have you ever felt that things people say or do in public, like conversations, songs on the radio, or things in the news, are secretly about you or have a special message for you?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I listen to the radio on my way to work sometimes, but it's just music, you know? Just regular songs. I'd never think they were about me. I'm just a regular guy, not a celebrity or anything! 

And the news... well, the news is always so depressing lately, I try not to watch it too much anyway. But when I do, it's just about what's going on in the world. It doesn't have anything to do with me. 

I know some people get really caught up in that kind of stuff, looking for signs everywhere, but I really try to stay grounded. I want to make sure I'm focused on reality, especially with my job. It's better to just take things at face value, right? I think that's the healthy way to look at it, don't you?

inference_history.note: The patient denied any thought insertion or thought broadcasting, ruling out delusional disorder (F22) and certain schizophrenia spectrum disorders with thought insertion/broadcasting features. However, the presence of disorganized thinking, mild paranoia, and possible formal thought disorder keeps schizophrenia spectrum and related disorders (F20, F21, F25) as possible differentials.

The patient denies hallucinations, thought insertion/broadcasting, and grandiose or bizarre delusions, ruling out schizophrenia (F20.0, F20.3, F20.4, F20.5, F20.6, F20.8, F20.9) and schizoaffective disorder (F25.0, F25.1, F25.2, F25.3, F25.8, F25.9). The presence of disorganized thinking, some degree of paranoia (non-bizarre delusional thinking about being watched), and difficulty with concentration raises the likelihood of other schizophrenia spectrum disorders such as F20.1 (disorganized type), F21 (schizotypal disorder), and F22 (persistent delusional disorder), though F22 remains less likely without a clear, circumscribed delusional theme.

The patient reported recent depressive symptoms including low mood, difficulty organizing daily tasks, social withdrawal, and suicidal ideation. This raises concern for a comorbid major depressive episode (F32.2), which was not previously indicated in the earlier dialogue. Schizophrenia (F20.1), schizotypal disorder (F21), and delusional disorder (F22) remain in the differential based on thought disorganization, tangential speech, and ideas of reference regarding supervisors, but the emergence of significant mood symptoms expands the differential to include major depression with psychotic features (F32.2).

Ruled out F20.1 (Schizophrenia, disorganized type) due to absence of prominent hallucinations, thought insertion/broadcasting, or grossly disorganized behavior. The presence of mood symptoms (e.g., suicidal ideation, low energy, difficulty concentrating) supports the inclusion of F32.2 (Major depressive disorder, recurrent, severe without psychotic features). F21 (Schizotypal disorder) remains due to odd thinking and ideas of reference (belief supervisors are watching), and F22 (Persistent delusional disorder) remains due to the non-bizarre delusional belief about being watched, though not fully elaborated. Further clarification is needed regarding mood symptoms and duration of thought disturbance.

This turn added F23.2 (Persistent delusional disorder) due to the patient's paranoid concern about being watched by supervisors, which appears to be a non-bizarre delusion. F20.1 (Disorganized type schizophrenia) remains a candidate due to the disorganized speech, thought process, and odd behaviors (e.g., imitation of patients, being 'stuck' mid-task). F32.3 (Major depressive disorder, severe with psychotic features) is considered due to the presence of severe depression, suicidal ideation, and possible mood-congruent delusions (e.g., belief that supervisors are specifically targeting them). Psychotic features in depression can sometimes present as paranoid concerns, particularly in the context of feeling judged or failing at responsibilities. The presence of mood symptoms and suicidal ideation makes F32.3 a strong candidate alongside psychotic disorders.

F23.2 was ruled out as there is no evidence of acute polymorphic psychotic disorder without symptoms like thought insertion, broadcast, or delusions of reference. F20.1 (Disorganized Schizophrenia) remains due to disorganized thinking, speech, and behavior. F32.3 (Major Depressive Disorder, Severe with Psychotic Features) remains due to severe depressive symptoms, possible psychomotor disturbance, and suicidal ideation without clear delusions or hallucinations. Further clarification is needed to confirm if psychotic features are present in depression or if disorganized schizophrenia is the better fit.
